title: Sequence slimming: adaptive token merge + prefill prioritization (Prefill Gambit)
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Deliver a micro-batching optimization that reduces padded tokens by performing lightweight, reversible token-level merging during prefill and applying a prioritized prefill queue. The approach (Prefill Gambit) combines: 1) a fast token-clustering pass that merges adjacent low-information tokens into compact placeholders for packing; 2) a per-microbatch kernel hint score that prefers kernel variants optimized for shorter effective sequence lengths; and 3) a prefill prioritizer that orders prefill vs decode work to maximize reuse of KV cache while respecting latency SLOs. The merged tokens are expanded deterministically before attention compute so model correctness is preserved. This ticket covers design, runtime changes to the request packer and kernel hint emitter, unit tests, and canary metrics.
acceptance_criteria: >=18% reduction in average padded tokens per microbatch on production trace A without exceeding 5% increase in 99th-percentile latency
Kernel hint selector emits per-batch kernel preference and gracefully falls back when kernel unsupported
Prefill prioritizer integrates with request-packer and honors per-request priority flags; toggled via Console feature flag
No token loss: sequence slimming must round-trip exactly (expanded tokens match original) validated by unit tests
Console dashboards added: padded-token savings, per-kernel usage breakdown, latency and cost delta charts
comments: 2026-02-10 - Initial spec created by Aisha Kumar. Outlines token-clustering algorithm (lightweight suffix/prefix coalescing) and kernel-hint scoring. Links: Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUN/Prefill+Gambit

2026-02-14 - Sync with Research: Jin Park ran microbenchmarks comparing merged-token expand-on-the-fly vs expand-before-attention. Expand-before-attention wins for latency on A100; memory checks ok for typical batches.

2026-02-18 - Design review (PM + Infra): agreed to make slimming conservative by default (only merge tokens below entropy threshold) to avoid hallucination risk. PM requested safe opt-out flag per-customer.

2026-02-22 - Engineering spike finished: prototype integrated into request-packer, observed 21% pad reduction on internal synthetic chat trace; 1.7% avg latency improvement, 4% tail latency regression on pathological long-prefix cases. Added kernel hint header (X-Kernel-Hint) in packer metadata.
2026-02-25 - PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4567 - implements token-cluster pass and kernel hint emitter. Needs perf tests and canary config.
2026-02-27 - PM feedback on customer controls: added console toggle + per-org opt-out setting. Security reviewed reversible expansion code; no secrets access required.

2026-03-01 - Perf run on production trace B: padded-token reduction 19.2% avg, cost estimate reduction ~12% (token billing model), 99p latency stable on default routing. Next: implement safe fallback that disables slimming when KV reuse drops below threshold.
Open questions: threshold tuning methodology across model families (decoder-only vs encoder-decoder), interaction with sparse attention kernels, and exact cost accounting for merged placeholders.
